## 3. The evidence that moved it



**Clinical AI acquired trial-grade evidence on the enthusiastic side.** An
eyecare foundation model was published as a
[randomized controlled trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40877476/) and a
generative-AI-discovered TNIK inhibitor reached a
[randomized phase 2a](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40461817/), while the
skeptical side of the month is two benchmarks of open-weight models. The caveat
is load-bearing and unresolved: a randomized AI trial is frequently randomized
on workflow or efficiency endpoints rather than on patient outcomes, and neither
abstract has been read.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-26"
    This section originally called August an *inversion* — the claim being that
    through spring the enthusiastic side had benchmarks while the skeptical side
    had randomized trials, and that August reversed it. The second half of that
    was never true. Re-reading January to July 2025 under one consistent rule
    found **zero** titles stating a null or negative result for any AI
    intervention in any month. Randomized AI trials existed from February
    ([GPT-4 assistance](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39910272/),
    [TAILORED-AF](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39953289/)) and none of them
    reported a null in its title. What spring actually had was a methodological
    critique — [*A benchmarking crisis in biomedical machine learning*](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40200055/),
    April 2025 — plus a single-cell foundation-model
    [limitations paper](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40251685/). Nothing
    inverted in August; the enthusiastic side gained, and the skeptical side was
    never where this corpus had recorded it.

**Microbiota-to-antitumour-immunity got a cell, not a taxon.**
[40659786](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40659786/) attributes microbiota-driven
antitumour immunity to dendritic cell migration. Most of what this corpus has
recorded on the microbiome-immunotherapy link is compositional correlation; this
is a trafficking mechanism, and it is the kind of result that decides whether
the thread survives contact with intervention trials.

**Cancer neuroscience was the crowded direction of the month** — three *Nature*
papers and two *Cell* papers, including
[nerve injury driving anti-PD-1 resistance](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40836096/),
which is the first time in this corpus the neural axis is joined to checkpoint
resistance. The reviewing agent flagged the cluster as peaking on the grounds
that it is entirely preclinical with zero clinical readouts. That call has now
been made three times on this thread and has been wrong three times. See the
note on `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` in `data/threads.yml`: a direction with
negative clinical readouts is failing, a direction with no clinical readouts is
untested, and the literature alone cannot tell them apart.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Nothing landed on a tracked thread with a title-stated direction this month
beyond the connectomics limit below. The month's large negative block — three
simultaneous aspirin-withdrawal trials, two beta-blocker-after-MI trials, and
antihypertensive deprescribing — sits in cardiology, outside the corpus fields,
and is recorded here only because it is the clearest de-escalation programme in
the eighteen months scanned.

### (b) Method credibility

Two *Nature* retractions in one month, both of anchors rather than minor papers:
the [Parkin/PINK1 restraint on STING-induced inflammation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40739362/)
and the [fetal cerebellar atlas](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40634621/) that
assigned medulloblastoma its cell of origin. A retracted cell-of-origin atlas is
worse than a retracted mechanism, because atlases are cited as reference rather
than as claim.

[40460825](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40460825/) (*Cell*) states a boundary
on the connectomics premise: structure-to-function prediction fails where
infrequent strong synapses dominate. It is filed under `foundation-models` as
well as `method-credibility`, because the assumption it limits — that a
sufficiently complete structural map predicts function — is the same assumption
under scaled models of biology generally.

[40866696](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40866696/) (*Nature*) refutes the
niche-limitation assumption in haematopoietic stem cell biology in its title.
